newsitem.title: UK: Treasuries steady in London, sentiment mixed.
newsitem.headline: Treasuries steady in London, sentiment mixed.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries held steady in London on Wednesday after their overnight rally following the Federal Reserve's decision to hold fire on interest rates.
But analysts said sentiment was mixed amid expectations of a future hike.

"The curve steepened up quite dramatically in the aftermath of the numbers," said Mark Weisbrod, government bonds trader at Daiwa Europe in London. The two-year note to 30-year bond spread was at 70 basis points by 1040 GMT, unchanged from the New York close.
"Sentiment is still quite mixed. The short end of the market particularly is good value as there won't be a rate rise at least until July," Weisbrod added.
The longer end of the curve bumped into resistance after the Federal Open Market Committe (FOMC) decision, suggesting investor concerns are high about a rate tightening when they next meet in July.
By 1040 GMT, the 30-year T-bond was at 96-16 yielding 6.90 percent, down from 96-18 in Tokyo and unchanged from New York.
The two-year note was at 100-10, yielding 6.20 percent, unchanged from both Tokyo and New York.

Weisbrod expected the two-year yield to rally to about 6.15 percent in the short run. The T-bond future meanwhile could be trapped in the 109-12 to 110-12 range for a while. By 1046 GMT the June T-bond was up 8/32 in automated trade at 110-03.

Michael Derks, fixed income strategist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, said despite the latest steepening, the Treasury curve was still flat and a lack of significant economic data in the next two weeks would keep the market subdued.
"There is not a huge amount there to be picked," he said.
Analysts said the dollar's bounce from its lows overnight would ultimately benefit Treasuries. By European mid-morning the dollar hovered around 114 yen after a low of 113.35.
